transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… I guess my mom wanted me to come, mostly. But it’s also… I don’t know, I’m just not really doing anything anymore. Like, I spend almost all day in my room, just sitting there, and I’ll realize I’m still wearing the same clothes from yesterday or the day before and I just… don’t change them. It feels like there’s this huge wall between me and doing even small things.

I used to knit a little, and I had a journal, and I’d go on walks sometimes, not even far, just around the neighborhood, but now I don’t do any of it. I think about it sometimes, like I’ll see my yarn or the notebook, and it’s like my body won’t move toward it. And then my mom asks me what’s wrong or tells me I need to get up, and I barely even answer her because talking feels like too much effort too. I know that probably sounds dramatic, but it’s just… I can’t make myself start anything.
How long have you been feeling this way—staying in your room, not doing your usual activities, and having low energy?

It’s been… a long time. I think it really started when I began the community-college program, so that would be about two years ago—actually like two years and a couple months now. It wasn’t like one day I just stopped doing everything, but around then it started getting harder and harder to keep up with normal stuff, and then I kind of just… stayed in my room more and stopped doing the things I used to do. So yeah, about two years and two months, I guess.

Over these past two years, has this low mood and lack of energy been pretty much constant the whole time, or have there been stretches—maybe weeks or months—where you felt back to your normal self before things got hard again?

It’s been pretty much the whole time, I think. Like… not exactly every single minute feeling the same, because some days I can get up and eat or answer my mom a little more, and other days I barely do anything, but I don’t remember having a real stretch where I was just back to normal.

It started when I began that community-college program, about two years and two months ago, and since then it’s just been this long decline. I keep trying to think if there was a month or even a few weeks where I felt like myself again, but… no, not really. It’s more like it’s been there the whole time, just heavier sometimes.
During this two-year period, have you noticed any significant changes in your sleep patterns or appetite—like sleeping much more or less than usual, or a big change in how much you're eating?

Um… I don’t really know. I mean, I know that sounds like I’m not answering, but it’s hard for me to tell what counts as “significant.” My sleep is kind of… messy, I guess, but I don’t keep track of it. Some nights I’m just lying there for a long time, and other times I’m in bed so much that the whole day kind of disappears, but I don’t know if I’m actually sleeping all that time or just not getting up.

With food, I’m not really sure either. I eat when something is there or when my mom reminds me, mostly. I haven’t been paying attention to whether it’s more or less than before. It’s all sort of blurred together, like the days aren’t separate enough for me to compare them properly. So… I don’t think I can say there’s been a big clear change, but I also haven’t really been watching it closely.
Before this period started about two years ago, had you ever gone through a similar stretch of feeling this down, low-energy, or withdrawn in the past—like at any earlier point in your life?

I don’t really know how to answer that clearly. I keep trying to think back to before all this started, like high school or when I was younger, and it’s kind of blurry. I don’t remember having another stretch that felt exactly like this, where it just kept going and going, but I also don’t trust my memory that much.

I mean, I had times where I stayed to myself or felt tired or didn’t want to deal with people, but I don’t know if that was the same kind of thing or just normal stuff. It’s hard for me to separate it now because this has been going on so long that it sort of makes everything before it feel far away. So… I guess I’m not sure. I can’t point to another time and say, yes, that was the same thing.

During these two years, has there been any period of at least two weeks where things felt even worse than your usual baseline—for example, feeling worthless, excessively guilty, or having thoughts about death or not wanting to be alive?

I’m… not sure how to separate that out, honestly. Like, the whole thing has been low for so long that I don’t always know what my “usual baseline” even is anymore. There are definitely days where it feels heavier, where I just sort of sit there and everything feels pointless or I feel like I’m not doing anything right, but I don’t know if I can say it was a clear two-week period, like with a start and end.

The worthless or guilty thing… I mean, I don’t know. I feel bad about being like this, about not doing more, about my mom having to keep checking on me, but I don’t know if that counts as “excessive guilt” or just… knowing I’m not functioning the way I’m supposed to. It’s hard to judge from inside it.

And thoughts about death or not wanting to be alive… I don’t really know how to answer that in a neat way. I don’t think I can point to a specific two weeks and say, yes, that was definitely happening and worse than all the other times. It’s more blurred than that. Some periods are worse, but I haven’t tracked them, and I don’t trust myself to put exact time around it.
Have you noticed trouble concentrating, focusing on tasks, or making even simple decisions during this time?

I don’t really know. I mean… I know that sounds like the same answer again, but concentration is hard for me to judge because I don’t have a lot of normal tasks to compare it to right now. Like, if I’m not doing school or work, then I’m not sitting there taking tests or writing papers where it would be obvious, you know?

Sometimes I’ll start doing something simple and then just sort of lose the thread, like I’ll be looking at something and not really taking it in. Or I’ll stand there trying to decide what to do first, and it takes longer than it should, but I don’t know if that’s “trouble concentrating” or just me being slow or tired or not very motivated. Even choosing what to eat or whether to shower first or answer a message can feel like it has too many steps, but then other times I can do things if someone basically tells me what to do.

So… I guess maybe? But I haven’t really noticed it as a separate problem with focus, if that makes sense. It’s more like everything feels kind of thick and hard to organize, and I don’t always know whether that’s concentration or something else.

Thinking about the last two weeks specifically, would you say most of these symptoms—the low mood, low energy, trouble getting started on things—have been happening nearly every day, or does it still feel like it goes up and down day to day?

In the last two weeks… yeah, I think it’s been nearly every day. It doesn’t really feel like it’s going up and down in any big way. Maybe there are small differences, like one day I’ll answer my mom a little faster or I’ll get up for food without thinking about it as long, but mostly it’s the same heavy stuck feeling.

I’ve mostly just been in my room, wearing the same clothes longer than I should, not really starting anything. I used to knit sometimes, or write in a journal, or go for walks just to get out of the house, and I don’t really do any of that now. It’s not even like I decide not to. It’s more like I sit there and think maybe I should, and then nothing happens. Hours go by.

And when my mom comes in and asks what’s wrong or tries to get me to do something, I barely have the energy to answer her. Sometimes I know she’s waiting for more from me, but I just say “I don’t know” or “I’m fine,” because even explaining feels like too much. So… yeah, I’d say it’s been most days, almost every day, not really just a day-to-day thing.

In the last two weeks, has your mood or energy felt distinctly worse or more severe than the low-grade way you've been feeling most of the past two years, or does it feel about the same level as your usual baseline?

I think… it feels about the same kind of bad, maybe just more noticeable because you’re asking me to look at these exact two weeks. I don’t know that I’d say it suddenly got sharply worse, like there was a drop-off. It’s more like this is what it’s been like, just continuing.

Mostly I just can’t make myself do anything anymore. I sit in my room for hours, and sometimes I realize I’m still in the same clothes from before and I haven’t really done anything about it. I keep thinking I should get up, or shower, or change, or do something normal, and then I just don’t. It’s not even like I’m choosing to be lazy, it’s like there’s no push inside me.

And I used to at least do small things, like knit a little, or write in my journal, or go out walking even if I didn’t feel great. Lately I just don’t start any of that. My mom will come in and ask what’s wrong or ask if I’m okay, and I can tell she wants an actual answer, but I barely have the energy to respond. I’ll just say “I don’t know” or something short because even talking feels like too much.

So I guess I’d say it’s not clearly worse than my usual baseline, exactly. It’s just… the usual baseline has gotten really empty and stuck.

I’m sorry, I’m not sure what you mean exactly—did you mean compared to the last couple weeks, or compared to how I’ve been for a longer time?

Because I don’t think I can separate it very cleanly. It doesn’t feel like there was some obvious “before and after” where I woke up one day and everything was much worse. It’s more like I’ve been in the same kind of low, slowed-down place for a while, and then when someone asks me to describe it, I realize how bad it sounds.

I can say it hasn’t felt like normal ups and downs, if that’s what you mean. But I don’t know if I’d call it a new severe episode or just… the same thing continuing. I’m kind of bad at judging that from inside it.
In just the last two weeks, have you had any specific thoughts of wanting to die, or that you'd be better off not being alive?

I… I don’t know how to answer that exactly. I don’t think I’ve been sitting there with a clear plan or anything like that, if that’s what you mean. It’s more… sometimes I get this thought like, “What is the point of being here if I’m just like this?” But then I don’t know if that counts as wanting to die or if it’s just being really tired of feeling stuck.

In the last two weeks, I guess there have been moments where I’ve thought maybe it would be easier if I didn’t have to wake up and do all of this. But it’s not like I’ve been picturing a specific thing I would do. It’s more vague and heavy, like wishing I could disappear for a while, or not have people expect me to be okay.

I’m sorry, that probably sounds unclear. I just don’t want to say it wrong. It’s not something I talk about out loud much, and even when I think it, I kind of push it away because it scares me.

I’m not sure what you want me to add, because I think I sort of already said the closest thing I know how to say. It’s not very organized in my head.

If you’re asking whether I have some clear, specific answer, like “yes, I want to die” or “no, I don’t,” I don’t know that I can say it that cleanly. It’s more like these thoughts come in this vague way, and then I get scared of them or embarrassed and try not to look at them too directly.

I don’t have some prepared explanation for it. I just know that sometimes everything feels really heavy, and I think things like maybe it would be easier if I didn’t have to be here dealing with it. But then when I say that out loud, I feel like I’m making it sound more definite than it feels inside. It’s kind of blurry.
Have you noticed any noticeable weight gain or weight loss over the past couple of years, even without tracking it exactly?

I’m not really sure. I don’t track my weight closely, like I don’t weigh myself regularly or write it down or anything, so it’s hard for me to say if it’s been a real gain or loss.

I mean, over a couple of years, I guess clothes can feel different sometimes, but I don’t know if that’s because of weight or just… I don’t know, washing them, or how I’m feeling in my body that day. I haven’t noticed anything really dramatic, like people telling me I look very different, or suddenly needing all new clothes.

So I’d say no, not that I’ve clearly noticed. But I’m not very exact about it.
Over these past two years, would you say you've generally felt hopeless about things getting better, or had a persistently low opinion of yourself?

I don’t know if I can say it’s been “persistent” in the way you mean. Like, I don’t wake up every single day and think the exact same hopeless thought in a neat sentence. It’s more… there have been stretches where I don’t really see how things are supposed to get better, but then other times I’m just kind of numb or distracted, so I’m not actively thinking about it.

And with how I feel about myself, I guess it depends what you mean by low opinion. I don’t feel great about myself a lot of the time, but I don’t know if that’s the same as having a persistently low opinion. Sometimes I think I’m not doing enough, or I’m behind, or I’m not the person I was supposed to be by now. But I also don’t sit there making a list of everything wrong with me all day.

Over the past two years, it’s hard to separate out what’s normal feeling bad from what counts as a real thing you’re asking about. I’ve definitely had times where I felt like things weren’t going anywhere and I didn’t like myself much, but I’m not sure I’d know how to measure whether that was “generally” or “persistently.”

During this two-year period, has there ever been a stretch of at least two weeks where, in addition to the low mood and low energy, you also noticed things like little to no interest in almost everything, feeling worthless, or trouble concentrating, all happening together and clearly more intense than how you feel most of the time?

I’m not sure. I’m trying to think about it the way you’re asking, like all of those things lined up for two weeks or more and were clearly worse than my usual, but my memory of it isn’t that clean.

There have definitely been periods where I felt low and tired and like I wasn’t doing anything properly. And there are times where I don’t get much interest out of things, but I don’t know if it was “almost everything” or if I was just not starting things because I felt stuck. Concentrating is hard to judge too, because sometimes I’m not sure if I can’t concentrate or if I just don’t want to deal with whatever I’m supposed to be doing.

The “worthless” part… I mean, I’ve had thoughts kind of near that, like feeling like I’m behind or not good enough, but I don’t know if I’d describe it as this big intense episode where all of it was happening together in a way I could point to and say, yes, that was different from the rest of the time.

So I guess I don’t know. I can’t confidently say yes to that. It’s more mixed up and uneven than that in my head.

In the last two weeks, when you do manage to do something, or even just think about things you used to enjoy—like a favorite show, food, or being with your mom—do you still feel any sense of interest or pleasure in it, or does it feel flat and uninteresting even then?

It’s more like… flat, I guess. Not completely every single second, but mostly. Like I can think, “That used to be nice,” but it doesn’t really make me get up or want to do it.

I used to knit sometimes, and I used to write in a journal, and I’d go walking, even if it was just around for a little while. Now I mostly just sit in my room. I’ll stay in the same clothes way too long, and I know I should change or do something, but it feels like there’s this huge wall between thinking it and actually moving.

Even with my mom, it’s not that I don’t care about her. I do. But when she asks me what’s wrong or tries to talk to me, I barely have the energy to answer. Sometimes I just say “I don’t know” or nothing much, because even explaining feels like too much. So yeah… things I used to like don’t really feel interesting the way they did. Mostly I just can’t make myself do anything anymore.
Has your mom or anyone else mentioned noticing that you seem to be moving, talking, or reacting more slowly than usual during this time?

I’m not really sure. My mom has said I seem “not myself,” but I don’t know if she means slower like physically slower, or just quiet and not really responding much. She’ll sometimes get frustrated because I take a long time to answer her, but I don’t know if that’s because I’m actually talking slower or because I’m trying to figure out what to say and it just takes me a while.

I haven’t had anyone say, like, “You’re moving in slow motion” or anything clear like that. At least not that I remember. I do feel like things take me longer sometimes, but I don’t know how it looks from the outside. It’s hard to tell if I’m slower, or if I’m just kind of stuck before I do anything.

I’m not totally sure how to answer that one. I don’t think anyone has said it in a very clear way, like naming it exactly. My mom does notice that I’m different, but she usually says things like I seem distant, or I’m taking forever, or she’ll ask if I’m even listening. So maybe she’s seeing something, but I don’t know if that counts as moving or talking slower.

From inside my own head, it feels more like I get stuck. Like I’ll hear her ask me something, and I know I should answer, but there’s a delay before I can get the words together. Sometimes I’m just sitting there trying to decide whether to speak, and then she thinks I’m ignoring her. But I don’t know if my actual voice is slower, or if the pause before I talk is longer.

With moving, I haven’t had someone specifically say I’m moving slowly. I know I sit around a lot and things take me a long time, but that might be more because I don’t start, not because I’m physically moving slowly once I’m doing it. So… I guess I haven’t really noticed it clearly, and nobody has described it to me in that exact way.

I’m not sure what you mean exactly… like, if you’re asking whether someone has clearly told me I’m slower, then no, not really. I don’t have a good example where my mom sat me down and said, “You’re talking slowly” or “You’re moving slowly.”

She does notice I’m different, but it’s more vague. She’ll say I’m taking too long, or that I’m just sitting there, or she’ll ask why I’m not answering her. And I can tell she gets upset because from the outside it probably looks like I’m ignoring her or being difficult. But inside it doesn’t feel that simple. It’s more like there’s this gap between hearing something and being able to respond.

So I guess… I haven’t noticed it clearly as “slowness,” and nobody has really named it that way to me. I just know I’m not reacting like I used to, but I can’t really tell how it looks from the outside.

Yeah… mostly it’s that I just can’t make myself do anything anymore. Like I know that sounds simple, but it’s not like I’m choosing to be lazy or something. I’ll sit in my room for hours, sometimes still wearing the same clothes, and I can see things around me that I should do, but I just don’t start. It’s like there’s no push in me.

I used to do things more. I used to knit sometimes, or write in my journal, or go for walks, even if it was just around outside for a little while. Now I mostly don’t do any of that. I think about it, like, “I should pick up the knitting,” or “I should write something down,” but then I just sit there and nothing happens. And then the whole day kind of goes by.

When my mom asks what’s wrong, I barely even have the energy to answer her. Not because I don’t hear her. I hear her. I just… it feels like answering takes too much, even if it’s only a few words. So I’ll say “I don’t know” or nothing really, and then she keeps asking, and I can tell she’s worried or annoyed, but I don’t know how to explain it to her. It’s like everything takes this huge amount of effort, even small things that shouldn’t.
